battle.title: Spread the Load
battle.description: Round robin, least connections and the hash that moves everyone.

questions.text: What is the main purpose of a load balancer in front of several servers?
options: Spread requests across servers for more capacity and availability
Make every request faster by compressing it
Store a copy of the database on each server
Replace the need for health checks
questions.answer: Spread requests across servers for more capacity and availability
questions.explanation: A load balancer distributes incoming traffic and stops routing to unhealthy servers, so you gain capacity and resilience. It does not speed up a single request, and it relies on health checks.

questions.text: What is a weakness of plain round robin?
options: It can only work with two servers
It always sends one client to the same server
It ignores each server's capacity and current load
It requires sessions to be stored in the balancer
questions.answer: It ignores each server's capacity and current load
questions.explanation: Round robin hands out requests in turn, so a slow or weak server gets the same share as a strong one even if it is already busy. Weighted or least-connections strategies address this.

questions.text: Requests vary hugely: some finish in 5 ms, others hold a connection for 30 seconds. Which balancing strategy suits this best?
options: Always the first server until it is full
questions.explanation: Least connections sends new work to the server with the fewest active connections, so servers stuck on long requests are avoided. Round robin and random keep feeding busy servers.

questions.text: Shopping carts live in each web server's memory, so users lose carts when a server restarts or is replaced. What is the best fix?
options: Use sticky sessions forever and hope servers stay up
Buy one bigger server and drop the balancer
Switch the balancer to round robin
Move sessions to a shared store such as Redis so any server can serve any user
questions.answer: Move sessions to a shared store such as Redis so any server can serve any user
questions.explanation: Sticky sessions hide the problem but carts still vanish when that server dies. A shared session store makes servers stateless and interchangeable. Round robin alone would scatter users across servers with no cart.

questions.text: Clients are mapped to servers with id % servers. How many of these six clients change server when the pool grows from 3 to 4? What does the program print?
questions.explanation: The program prints 4: ids 7, 20, 33 and 41 move, while 12 and 50 stay. Plain hash-mod remaps most clients when the pool size changes, which is why consistent hashing is used when remapping is expensive.
